requirements.quote: `forgedock orchestrate --select '<query>'` (for example `no:milestone`, `milestone:X`, `label:Y`) stores the selector in the batch.
Every few minutes the runner reconciles: matching open issues join (under the same DAG, priority and lane rules); closed or moved issues leave.
That replaces issue-watch for this use; no separate process is needed.
An issue stays scheduled until it's closed, merged, or blocked by a **human code** (credentials, spend, customer, promotion, product decision).
`deferred`/"gave up" → retried with exponential backoff (cap about 2 h), not dropped;
`held` on an engine error → re-admitted on any **agent/lane-image** version change, not only a dispatcher change, and after a cooldown (for example 6 h) as a fresh attempt;
env-held → the engine's `env.*` issue joins the same order automatically, and its closure re-admits the waiters (this exists for closure; the joining is missing);
conformance failures → one more recovery attempt after the base moves (new staging commits) before parking, and the parked issue is listed in a single "needs decision" digest instead of being lost.
The breaker auto-resets after a cooldown when the failure signature was environmental (VM restart, mirror, network) and the pool is healthy again (#5947 classes), with a FORGE:DECISION on the batch.

requirements.why: owned by #5966 (already merged); this change only relies on the schedd hosting the reconcile tick

requirements.quote: For a staging lane, close the issue on merge into the lane branch (`Closes` doesn't fire there), and fold any post-deploy checks into the release checklist rollup (`postdeploy_rollup`).

`forgedock orchestrate --status <id>` shows the order's coverage: matching open issues = running + queued + backing-off + waiting on deps + human-blocked (list), with **0 "unscheduled"** as the healthy state.
A new issue matching the selector joins within one reconcile interval, with no watcher process. Covered by a test.
An issue that ends `deferred`/`held`/`engine-error` is re-admitted automatically (backoff, agent version change, or cooldown) with no operator command. Covered by a test.
Engine-filed `env.*` issues join the same order. Covered by a test.
`--status` reports 0 unscheduled for a healthy order; the only issues outside running/queued/backoff are human-coded.
Post-deploy: the AlterLab no-milestone order runs 24 h with zero operator commands while open issues trend to the human-blocked floor.
requirements.why: only measurable on the live AlterLab batch for 24 h after release

deliverables.change: persist the selector in batch state (`select` field); add a coverage classifier (running/queued/backing-off/waiting-deps/human-blocked/unscheduled) shared with --status

new module: selector search via gh, diff against batch membership (join matching open issues, leave closed/moved), re-admission policy (deferred backoff cap 2h, held on agent/lane-image version change or 6h cooldown, conformance one retry after base moves, needs-decision digest), env.* join, human-code classification

call reconcile on an interval through the existing add/requeue seams (same DAG, priority, lane rules); register engine-filed env.* issues into the batch; breaker auto-reset after cooldown for environmental signatures with a FORGE:DECISION; close the issue on merge into a staging lane branch and fold post-deploy checks into the rollup
export an auto-reset decision (environmental signature + cooldown + pool healthy) alongside decideClear
host the reconcile tick for a selector batch so no separate watcher process is needed (no liveness change)
parse `--select <query>` on orchestrate start and `--status <id>` (coverage output, unscheduled count, human-blocked list); update ORCH_USAGE
document selector-backed standing orders, re-admission paths and --status

new tests: selector join within one interval, leave on close/move, deferred/held/engine-error re-admission, env.* join, conformance retry + digest, breaker auto-reset, staging-lane close, --status 0 unscheduled
tests for selector persistence and coverage classifier
